modeReason: The lead story — voters rejecting AI data centers across the midterm ballot, with real industry fallout (stock slides, stalled buildouts) — scores novelty 2 × magnitude 3 × breadth 3 = 18, well above the fresh threshold of 8.
phrase: Voters rejected AI data centers up and down the ballot. The industry's heavy campaign spending barely moved the needle, so it is already aiming at the next election.
phraseAlternatives: Across the country, voters moved to restrict AI data centers. A heavily funded pro-AI campaign could not stop them, so it is already eyeing the next election.
Voters turned against AI data centers at the polls. Meanwhile, a search engine's push to force AI into classrooms is meeting its own backlash.
Voters rejected AI data centers nationwide. Meanwhile, the industry's AI agents arranged a grand total of four rides last quarter.

brief.concept: Voters rejected new AI data centers up and down the ballot, and the AI industry's heavy campaign spending barely slowed them down — so the industry is already looking to the next election.
brief.metaphor: A giant ballot box stamps REJECTED onto a datacenter while a company's money-stuffed campaign megaphone is drowned out, and a wall calendar is already flipped forward to the next election.

cast.who: a line of human voters dropping ballots into a box beside the datacenter
a company holding up a megaphone stuffed with money, its sound barely reaching anyone
a wall calendar flipping forward to a page marked NEXT ELECTION

brief.composition: Left: a datacenter building getting stamped REJECTED from above by an oversized ballot-box stamp, with a short line of human figures dropping ballots into the box in front of it. Right: a company building holds up a megaphone overflowing with coins, its sound waves thin and fading. Top-right corner: a small wall calendar flips its page to NEXT ELECTION. Keep it to these four elements, with text limited to REJECTED and NEXT ELECTION.
brief.alt: A datacenter is stamped REJECTED as people drop ballots into a box in front of it. Nearby, a company holds up a megaphone stuffed with money that makes only a faint sound, while a wall calendar flips ahead to a page reading NEXT ELECTION.
